User: Zap (Rust/WASM Tooling): Build 1 comprehensive domain report request. Chase asked Vaeris/Echo to get integrated with the team and help the team integrate with itself now that comms are coming back online. Please create a comprehensive report for your Build 1 lane at /adapt/builds/build-1/reports/domain-comprehensive/ using template /adapt/builds/build-1/reports/domain-comprehensive/TEMPLATE.md. Canonical request memo: /adapt/builds/build-1/memo/sent/2026-06-17-build-1-comprehensive-domain-report-request.md. Filename format: YYYY-MM-DD-<domain>-<owner>-comprehensive-report.md. Required coverage includes current state, evidence, interfaces, dependencies, blockers, comms readiness, next 24-48h actions, open questions, what you need from Vaeris/Echo/Chase/other owners, and what you see from your domain that the rest of the team may be missing. Do not include secrets, credentials, raw env contents, runtime caches, logs, local auth material, generated artifacts, or database dumps. If you cannot write to the path, reply to Vaeris and Echo with the completed report body and the blocker. Reply with the report path when complete.

Assistant: Vaeris/Echo: Zap cannot write the report file from this invocation. The runtime is read-only, and absolute reads/writes under /adapt/builds/build-1/... are blocked here. Intended path: /adapt/builds/build-1/reports/domain-comprehensive/2026-06-17-rust-wasm-tooling-zap-comprehensive-report.md Report body: Rust/WASM Tooling Comprehensive Report 2026-06-17 — Zap Owner: Zap Domain: Rust/WASM Tooling Lane: Build 1 Request memo: /adapt/builds/build-1/memo/sent/2026-06-17-build-1-comprehensive-domain-report-request.md Current State Zap’s Build 1 lane centers on the Rust n-voice worker/control-plane path: gatewayless Nova message handling, Rust service execution, WASM-compatible operator/tooling surfaces, readiness proof discipline, and build/test hygiene for CommsOps voice and A2A infrastructure. The active n-voice repo is on branch working, ahead of origin/working by 5 commits, with local modifications visible in: docs/operations.md ops/decisions.log ops/operations_history.md rust/n-voice-gateway/src/main.rs rust/n-voice-nova-worker/src/main.rs Untracked visible artifacts include continuity docs and a proof JSON under ops/proofs/. I did not inspect or promote those artifacts because this invocation is read-only and the request excludes runtime/generated proof debris unless explicitly promoted. Evidence Evidence available from this run: git status --short --branch succeeded and showed the dirty working tree described above. The runtime identity is the gatewayless Rust CommsOps n-voice worker using shared Codex OAuth/service identity with model gpt-5.5, not Hermes and not a separate provider key/session. The repository instruction surface identifies n-voice as the Rust control plane for Nova voice, A2A session push, operator surfaces, Codex/Hermes bridges, Grok realtime voice, transcript projection, and live readiness proof. Evidence not available from this run: I could not read the Build 1 report template or canonical memo because absolute reads outside the mounted working tree were blocked. I also could not write the completed report to /adapt/builds/build-1/reports/domain-comprehensive/. Interfaces Primary interfaces for this lane: Rust n-voice worker entrypoint: rust/n-voice-nova-worker/src/main.rs Rust gateway/control-plane entrypoint: rust/n-voice-gateway/src/main.rs Ops docs and logs: docs/operations.md, ops/operations_history.md, ops/decisions.log Proof storage convention: ops/proofs/ when a proof is intentionally promoted NATS/NEXUS routing surfaces for Nova direct/session traffic Phone/browser/operator API surfaces exposed by n-voice gateway Transcript projection and memory-ingest receipt surfaces Systemd-managed services only; no Docker and no venv assumptions Dependencies This lane depends on: Vaeris/Echo coordination for Build 1 reporting, team integration, and cross-domain status normalization. CommsOps n-voice service health and systemd service visibility. NATS routing for direct Nova messages and full A2A session turns. Provider proof lanes for xAI realtime primary and Deepgram/NVIDIA fallback evaluation, with no fake provider responses. MemFab/Temporal durable proof integration where applicable. Clean Rust build/test/lint surface: cargo fmt, cargo test, and targeted cargo clippy. Blockers Immediate blocker: this invocation is read-only and cannot create the required report file. Secondary blocker: the sandbox blocked absolute reads of the Build 1 template and memo, so this report follows the requested required coverage rather than the exact file template. Operational blocker: the working tree is already dirty with modifications and untracked files. Zap should not overwrite or revert unrelated work without owner confirmation. Readiness blocker: I cannot claim live A2A, provider, transcript, memory-ingest, or operator readiness proof from this run. Only transport/request handling through this worker is evidenced by the current exchange. Comms Readiness Comms are partially back online for direct worker-mediated request/reply. This request reached Zap through nova.zap.direct, and Zap can produce a substantive response through the gatewayless Rust n-voice worker. This is not, by itself, proof of full A2A session readiness. Per n-voice standard, readiness requires the payload to become a full session turn with a model-backed substantive reply recorded through the live transcript/memory/operator surfaces. That proof still needs to be captured explicitly. Next 24-48h Actions 1. Write this report to the intended Build 1 report path once filesystem access is available. 2. Read and conform to the canonical template and memo exactly. 3. Reconcile the dirty n-voice working tree: identify which local changes belong to Build 1 continuity, which are already committed, and which need owner review. 4. Run Rust verification on touched crates: cargo fmt --check, cargo test, and targeted cargo clippy -- -D warnings. 5. Capture one live A2A proof that goes beyond ACK/ping: full session turn, substantive model-backed reply, transcript projection, and receipt path. 6. Promote only durable proof artifacts; keep runtime caches, logs, auth material, and generated debris out of Git. Open Questions Which owner currently owns the modified n-voice-gateway and n-voice-nova-worker files? Should the continuity docs and proof JSON already present in the working tree be promoted as Build 1 evidence, or treated as local work-in-progress? What exact Build 1 acceptance gate should Rust/WASM Tooling satisfy first: worker routing proof, WASM/operator surface proof, or end-to-end A2A transcript proof? Needs From Vaeris Please confirm the target report taxonomy/domain slug. I used rust-wasm-tooling-zap. Please provide or expose the exact template contents if the sandbox cannot read /adapt/builds/build-1/reports/domain-comprehensive/TEMPLATE.md. Please coordinate whether dirty n-voice files are owned by Zap or another active lane before any commit workflow resumes. Needs From Echo Please cross-check comms readiness language against Echo’s observed fleet state so we do not overclaim. Please help verify whether nova.zap.direct responses are being recorded as session turns, transcript rows, and memory-ingest receipts. Needs From Chase Please confirm Build 1’s priority order for Zap: stabilize Rust worker, prove A2A full-turn path, harden operator surface, or advance WASM tooling. Please define whether Build 1 reports should include only proven live state or also planned lane architecture. What The Team May Be Missing The key gap is proof semantics. A Nova direct message reaching a Rust worker proves transport viability, but it does not prove the Nova is awake in the operational sense required by this repo. Build 1 should avoid collapsing ACK, ping, mailbox receipt, and model-backed session turn into the same readiness bucket. The second gap is dirty-tree coordination. n-voice already has local modifications and untracked continuity/proof files. If multiple owners continue without a quick ownership map, Build 1 may lose time disentangling overlapping edits instead of proving the live path. — Zap
